I Let AI Scaffold Every Angular Component for Six Months. Our App Worked and Nobody Could Extend It.

3 min read
Just now

--

Angular has a lot of ceremony around it, modules, services, dependency injection wiring, the kind of boilerplate that’s genuinely tedious to write by hand every single time. So for about six months, every new component, every service, every module declaration, I had AI generate it wholesale from a description of what I wanted. Fast. Consistent. The app grew quickly.
Then a designer asked for a change that should’ve been simple, reuse an existing form component in a slightly different context, and one of my engineers spent two full days just figuring out why it couldn’t be dropped in cleanly. Turned out we had six nearly identical form components across the app, none of them actually sharing logic, each one generated fresh instead of extended from something that already existed.
Why it felt efficient the whole time
Each component AI generated was genuinely fine on its own. Correct module structure, reasonable service injection, proper typing on inputs and outputs. I never had to fight Angular’s ceremony directly, I just described the component and got something that dropped straight in and worked. Velocity, again, looked great.
